title: Senior Director, SEC Financial Reporting
description:
GrubMarket is seeking a Senior Director of SEC Financial Reporting to lead external financial reporting as the company prepares for life as a public company. GrubMarket operates across the food supply chain, combining food distribution with technology and software, and has announced the confidential submission of a draft registration statement on Form S-1 for a proposed public offering.

This role will own the accuracy, clarity, and timely delivery of SEC financial disclosures. The successful candidate will be a hands-on leader who can work across a complex group of businesses, build a durable reporting process, and partner effectively with accounting leadership, operations, legal counsel, and external auditors.

What you’ll do
Lead the preparation and review of the S-1 and related amendments, including financial statements, footnotes, MD&A, selected financial data, and responses to SEC comments.
Establish and manage the reporting calendar and processes for future Forms 10-K, 10-Q, and other applicable SEC filings.
Own financial statement tie-outs, disclosure checklists, supporting schedules, and the review of financial information presented throughout filings and investor materials.
Partner with corporate accounting and regional finance teams to ensure consolidated results are complete, consistent, and supported across acquired businesses and multiple accounting systems.
Draft and review technical accounting memoranda and disclosures for significant or complex transactions, including acquisitions, revenue recognition, debt, equity compensation, and other matters relevant to the business.
Coordinate with external auditors, legal counsel, and other advisers through filing preparation, audit and review cycles, and SEC comment resolution.
Lead the review of non-GAAP measures and operating metrics, ensuring clear definitions, consistent calculations, appropriate reconciliations, and documented support.
Develop reporting controls, documentation standards, and review procedures that support accurate, repeatable public company reporting.
Oversee the reporting workstream for new acquisitions, including the financial information and disclosures needed for consolidated reporting.
Build and develop a strong SEC reporting team as the company’s needs evolve.

What you bring
CPA designation and a bachelor’s degree in accounting or a related field.
Significant experience in SEC reporting and U.S. GAAP, including direct responsibility for preparing or reviewing Forms 10-K, 10-Q, or S-1.
Experience leading reporting for a public company or guiding a company through an IPO readiness process.
Strong technical accounting judgment and the ability to turn complex analyses into clear, well-supported disclosures.
Experience working with external auditors and legal counsel under demanding filing deadlines.
The ability to organize information across multiple entities, teams, and accounting systems.
A practical, detail-oriented leadership style and a willingness to work directly in the numbers and disclosures.

Experience with acquisition-heavy businesses, consolidations, XBRL, or financial reporting systems is a plus.
